HDB Resale Flat Prices Insight Pipeline

Event-driven Iceberg lakehouse on AWS
Set PROJECT_NAME before running setup.sh — hdb-dev / hdb-uat / hdb-eventdriven (prod)

1. Set up ~5 min

  1. Log in to AWS (console or CLI) with an account that can create IAM roles, S3 buckets, Glue jobs, Step Functions, Lambda, SNS, and optionally SES.
  2. Go to the deployment scripts: 
    cd hdb_1/pipeline-scripts/infrastructure_files/03_bash_scripts
  3. Choose an environment and, optionally, an alert email: 
    export PROJECT_NAME=hdb-eventdriven
export HDB_ALERT_RECIPIENT_EMAILS=you@example.com
export AWS_PROFILE=your-profile   # if not using the default
  4. Run it: 
    ./setup.sh
  5. Wait for SETUP COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY. If you set an alert email, confirm the SNS subscription from your inbox.
What gets created 6 Iceberg-backed S3 buckets, a Glue database, 6 Glue jobs plus 1 compaction job, a Step Functions state machine, 3 EventBridge rules, 1 Lambda, an SNS topic (+ SES), and 4 IAM roles — all scoped to $PROJECT_NAME, so dev/uat/prod never collide.

2. Verify the deployment

Resource names below assume PROJECT_NAME=hdb-eventdriven.

3. Run the pipeline

Option A — start the ingestion job

aws glue start-job-run --job-name hdb-job-1-ingestion-to-source

Once it succeeds, the ingestion-complete-trigger rule fires and runs job_2 through job_5 automatically.

Option B — drop a file (real production trigger)

Upload any file to s3://<bucket>/resale-flat-prices-manual-upload/

The S3 event fires EventBridge, which starts Step Functions — no CLI command needed.

Watch it run

  • Step Functions → hdb-eventdriven-pipeline → newest execution — watch each state turn green (job_2 → job_2b profiling → job_3 → job_4 → job_5 → compaction)
  • or Glue → ETL Jobs → any hdb-job-* → Runs tab, for one step at a time
Timing A full run through all 6 jobs usually takes several minutes, depending on how much data.gov.sg returns for the configured date range.

4. Check the results

In S3

  • *-raw / *-cleaned / *-transformed / *-hashed — Iceberg metadata + Parquet data for each layer
  • *-audit-tables — audit_iceberg, plus every alert email saved as alert-logs/success|failure/*.md (failed_iceberg lives in *-failed)

Three ways to read the run report

1Generate a log on demand — queries the pipeline tables live:

cd pipeline-scripts/06_reporting
python generate_run_log.py

2Pull the Markdown report Step Functions already saved:

aws s3 cp s3://mission-hdb-eventdriven-<account_id>-audit-tables/alert-logs/success/<execution-name>.md .

Swap success for failure after a failed run.

3Pull the saved HTML report:

aws s3 cp s3://mission-hdb-eventdriven-<account_id>-audit-tables/alert-logs/success/<execution-name>.html .

The exact HTML the email renders.

On success: a row per layer (status, records, rejected, duration), a reject-reason breakdown, and total run time. On failure: the exact step and Glue job that failed, the error message, and a link to the execution, ready to redrive.

Tear down ~2 min

Run this when you're done S3, Glue, and CloudWatch logs all bill while resources exist. 
cd hdb_1/pipeline-scripts/infrastructure_files/03_bash_scripts
PROJECT_NAME=hdb-eventdriven ./tear_down.sh

Removes Glue jobs, Step Functions, Lambda, IAM roles, EventBridge rules, and Athena resources — and, with confirmation, the S3 buckets and their data. The SNS topic and email subscription are kept, so re-running setup.sh later doesn't need re-confirming.

Sample outcome

What the report looks like on a real run — a clean pass on the left, a failed step on the right.

Architecture

End to end: ingestion trigger → Step Functions orchestration across the five Glue jobs → Iceberg data zones → reporting, notifications, and logging.

What this demonstrates

  • Genuinely event-driven — file arrival or job completion triggers the next stage, no polling
  • Step Functions with per-step redrive — a failure resumes where it stopped
  • A layered Iceberg lakehouse (source → raw → cleaned → transformed → hashed) with real MERGE INTO, time travel, and schema evolution
  • Operational visibility — row counts, rejection reasons, and per-job duration in the alert an on-call engineer would read
  • Multi-environment from one codebase — dev/uat/prod are just different PROJECT_NAME values
